title: Customer-facing service resilience update and FAQ (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a customer-facing draft that can be posted to the status page and sent to impacted customers after review. It combines a concise status update for a public-facing timeline with a short post-incident summary, recommended customer actions, and an FAQ tailored for product and platform engineers integrating with Redwood’s inference endpoints.

Key points (TL;DR):
- Window: 2028-11-17 23:40 UTC — 2028-11-18 03:12 UTC.
- Impact: Intermittent failed streaming responses and a small number of duplicate partial tokens for requests to the hosted generation endpoints (/v1/generate and streaming).
- Scope: ~1.8% of requests routed through a single regional routing pool experienced degraded responses. No customer data exfiltration or unauthorized access was detected.
- Action we took: automated routing rollback, targeted worker restart, and a KV-cache invalidation policy deployed.
- Recommended customer action: if you saw truncated or duplicate tokens, retry with idempotency_key and verify response completeness. See recommended client-side strategy below.

Public status-page entry (short form) — use for the status page update: 
Title: Intermittent streaming failures and duplicate partial tokens — Resolved
Impact: Between 2028-11-17 23:40 UTC and 2028-11-18 03:12 UTC some requests to Redwood hosted generation endpoints returned truncated or duplicated token fragments during streaming. Customers may have observed incomplete outputs or minor duplication.
Current status: Resolved — full service restored and routing pool removed from circulation pending engineering validation.
What we did: Rolled back a routing change that routed traffic into an experimental pool, restarted affected workers, and deployed a KV-cache invalidation fix.
What we’re doing next: Running an extended validation sweep of routing telemetry, adding additional checks to prevent similar routing pool misclassification, and adding customer-visible guardrails for streaming completeness.

Customer post-incident summary (concise) — suitable for email or support portal: 
Summary: On 2028-11-17 at ~23:40 UTC, a routing change combined with a stale KV cache state in one regional pool caused a subset of streaming sessions to deliver incomplete or duplicated token fragments. The root cause was an interaction between routing heuristics and a cache eviction race in the worker process.
Root cause (short): Two simultaneous changes — an experimental routing pool being promoted and an adjusted cache-eviction TTL — resulted in a small set of workers serving responses while holding inconsistent KV cache pointers. This produced truncated streaming frames and, in rare cases, token duplication when a session retried mid-stream.
Mitigation steps performed:
- Immediate rollback of the routing promotion to keep traffic on validated pools.
- Targeted restart of 42 worker processes in the affected region.
- Deployed an emergency fix that forces KV-cache pointer reconciliation on worker startup.
- Replayed affected telemetry to reconstruct request traces for impacted customers and initiated case outreach for those with >2% error surface.

Customer impact and scope:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (streaming), SDK streaming helpers.
- Percent of traffic affected: ~1.8% of requests globally during the window, concentrated in eu-west-1 region.
- Data confidentiality: No evidence of data exposure. Logs and traces were accessed only by on-call SRE and engineers during remediation.

Suggested short instructions for customers (for support or status page expansions):
If you observed truncated streaming output:
1) Retry the request once. If you control the client, set an idempotency_key per logical prompt to avoid duplicate side-effects.
2) For streaming clients, validate the final event ("done"/EOS) rather than assuming completion purely from connection close.
3) If partial duplication occurred, de-duplicate at the application layer using sequence heuristics (token prefix comparison) or idempotency tracking.

If your integration uses long-lived streaming sessions:
- Consider adding an application-level ACK (e.g., send a small heartbeat/ping every 30s) so your client can detect mid-stream reconnections and resume or retry cleanly.

Preventive/longer-term changes we’re implementing:
- Routing guardrails: additional telemetry thresholds before a pool promotion (min-health checks & warm-up quotas).
- Cache hardening: stronger reconciliation on worker startup and conservative eviction grace windows for streaming sessions.
- Improved agent-level checks: SDKs will include optional streaming-integrity helpers and recommended client-side idempotency patching examples.
- Post-deploy checklist updates: a mandatory staging soak for routing promotions affecting >0.5% of traffic.

Customer communication playbook (recommended flow):
- Status page: publish short form immediately (use above short form).
- Targeted customer outreach: for customers with automated monitors that saw >1% error surface, CS to open cases and send the concise post-incident summary with trace attachments.
- Postmortem: publish a sanitized technical postmortem (link) within 7 business days and a detailed remediation timeline within 30 days.

FAQ (customer-facing):
Q: Could this have caused my data to be seen by others?
A: No. We have no evidence of data leakage or access by unauthorized parties. Access to logs and traces was limited to the incident response team and only used for remediation.

Q: Will you compensate for errors or SLA breaches?
A: For customers impacted above their SLA thresholds, our support team will follow standard SLO/credit procedures once affected usage is verified. Please open a support case referencing SUP-3421.

Q: I rely on streaming for low-latency UX. Should I change anything now?
A: No immediate action required. We recommend adding idempotency keys and verifying explicit EOS markers in your client. We are releasing SDK helpers to make this easier.

Q: How can I check if my account was impacted?
A: If your monitoring booked >1% client error increase to streaming endpoints during the window, we’ve proactively created a support case and will reach out. You can also open SUP-3421 with your request ids for our team to verify.

Status page message (long form / expanded) — for internal use as the next update after the short resolution post: 
We discovered the incident was triggered by an unintentional promotion of traffic to an experimental regional routing pool at the same time an internal cache-eviction tuning was applied. The combination surfaced an eviction/lookup race that affected the KV-cache pointers used by the streaming runtime. When a worker served a streaming session with inconsistent cache pointers it occasionally emitted truncated frames or duplicated partial tokens if a session retried mid-stream.
Actions taken: rollback of the routing change, worker restarts, KV reconciliation fix, telemetry replay, and targeted customer outreach.
Next steps: additional routing safety checks (deploying), SDK streaming-integrity helpers (ETA 3 weeks), and a public technical postmortem with sanitized traces (ETA 7 days).

Suggested email template for impacted customers (short):
Subject: Update on your requests during Nov 17 outage — Redwood Inference
Hi <CustomerName>,
We recently identified an incident that impacted a small percentage of streaming generation requests on Nov 17 between 23:40–03:12 UTC. You may have observed truncated output or duplicated partial tokens. We’ve resolved the root cause and applied mitigations; no data exposure occurred. If you need a detailed trace for specific request ids, reply with the request ids and we’ll attach sanitized traces to your support case.
Thanks for your patience,
Evelyn Zhang
Customer Success (Redwood Inference)

Internal notes (things to confirm before publishing):
- Confirm legal review for phrasing re: data exposure.
- Confirm SLA credit process triggers for customers exceeding thresholds.
- Coordinate with SDK/Developer Experience on streaming-integrity helper ETA.
- Triage list of customers with >1% error surface for targeted outreach.

Version notes: 0.1 — initial draft for CS+SRE review.

Unresolved questions / follow-ups:
- Are there any older clients that do not surface EOS markers that we should contact proactively? (action: DX to run a client-version sweep by 2028-11-21)
- Can product add a per-pool "warm-up" metric visible in console by 2028-12-05? (action: Product + Observability)
- Confirm whether the KV reconciliation fix needs formal QA in private deployments (action: Eng-Platform).

End of draft.
summary: Draft status page entry, concise post-incident summary for customers, recommended mitigation steps and FAQ for an intermittent streaming/truncation incident affecting ~1.8% of traffic in eu-west-1.
